text:
A: Hiya! Oh, it's you! I said when I saw your photo, she looks a lot like me. Is that a terrible thing to say?
B: No, not at all. I thought something similar, actually. The cardigan, the kitchen.
A: Ha! Uniform of women our age, isn't it. I'm Joanne, Taunton.
B: Annelies. Sheffield.
A: Oh, lovely. Have you had a nice time with these? I've been chatting away to everyone, poor things.
B: Yes, they've been nice. I spoke to Helen just now, the archivist. We talked about books mostly.
A: Oh, she's lovely, isn't she? Quiet, but she's got a proper dry sense of humour once you get her going. She let me count ABBA as a hymn.
B: She was very kind about my watercolours. Which they don't deserve.
A: Oh, I bet they're better than you say. You've got the bird feeder, haven't you, I saw it in your window. Get much on it?
B: A robin, lately. He comes every morning about half seven, while I'm having my tea. Sorry, my cup of tea, I mean, not my meal. I've been in Yorkshire too long.
A: No, I'm the same, I say tea and dinner and nobody knows what I'm on about. Where are you from originally?
B: The Netherlands. Amersfoort. More than thirty years ago now.
A: Gosh. Do you still have family over there?
B: My sister. And my mother. She's in the early stages of dementia, erm, so I go over when I can. It's not easy, being on the ferry every time something happens.
A: Oh, love. My mum's starting with it too. Little things, you know, she put the kettle in the fridge last month and laughed it off, but I could see she was frightened. And I'm only forty minutes away and I still feel like I'm not doing enough. So goodness knows how you manage it from another country.
B: Badly, some weeks. I feel guilty a lot. My sister does most of it.
A: I don't think you should feel guilty. You're ringing, you're going over. That's not nothing. Sorry, I don't mean to tell you how to feel.
B: No, it's kind. Thank you. It's nice to hear it from someone who knows.
A: Do you go to church at all? Sorry, that's a nosy one. It's just it helps me, sort of, sitting there.
B: Yes, most Sundays. I don't say much about it. But I think it helps me too.
A: Same. I'm on the flower rota, which is mostly an excuse for coffee and gossip, if I'm honest.
B: I bake for ours. A Dutch apple cake. It disappears very quickly.
A: Oh, I'd love that recipe! I do traybakes. Lemon drizzle, millionaire's shortbread. I take them to choir and all.
B: You sing?
A: Community choir. Pop, musicals. Nothing like the proper stuff.
B: I listen to choral music on Radio 3. I cry at it, which is embarrassing.
A: Oh, I cry at Strictly results, so you're doing better than me!
B: I think we're nearly finished. It went fast.
A: It did. You take care of yourself, won't you?
